subject: Post-demo: Latency qualification & hosted vs current provider next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@streamlytics.com>, Dana Owens <dana.owens@streamlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Latency qualification & next steps (hosted vs your current provider)

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and very helpful context on Streamlytics' realtime ingestion workloads. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same checklist: 

1) Target SLOs (what we heard)
  - p95 end-to-end (client to response): 120ms for short requests (~64 tokens)
  - p99 end-to-end: 320ms
  - Sustained throughput: 200 reqs/sec (with bursts to 800 reqs/sec)
  - Streaming concurrency: up to 40 concurrent streamed responses

2) Primary unknowns we agreed to validate
  - Whether your current provider's e2e numbers account for client-side parsing and Kafka ingestion overhead
  - How p99 behaves under your real shard distribution and varying prompt lengths
  - Streaming tail latencies for long-lived responses (>=1024 tokens)

3) Proposed short-term plan (this week)
  - Redwood provides a short checklist + sample harness (attachment: redwood-latency-checklist.xlsx) for one-hour smoke tests against our hosted API
  - Streamlytics to run the harness against current provider and Redwood hosted endpoints and return the sample logs (hosted-vs-current-latency-sample.json)
  - Marissa will coordinate a 60‑minute joint run we can observe (can be remote screen-share)

4) Ownership
  - Redwood: deliver checklist, test harness, and a minimal doc describing streaming concurrency knobs
  - Streamlytics: run the harness, attach logs, and note any client-side instrumentation details (SDK versions, Kafka consumer lag metrics)

Can Marissa and Samir align on availability for the joint run? I penciled Wed/Thu next week on the MAP.

Thanks — Aisha

--
Aisha Rahman

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our "current provider" numbers are measured from the API gateway (so they exclude some of our Kafka ingest and downstream enrichment steps). We'll attach our gateway-side traces but we also plan to run the harness end-to-end like you suggested.
- The p95 target of 120ms is aggressive but possible for the short prompt profile; p99 will be the real test.
- For streaming: we typically have 30-45 concurrent client streams during peak. We can throttle to 40 for the run.

We're available Thursday (2026-07-16) 09:00-11:00 PT for the joint run. Samir

Thanks Samir — we'll take the 09:00-10:00 PT slot and observe the full run. A couple of technical notes (quick):

- The checklist includes two harness modes: (1) short-request mode (64–128 tokens) and (2) streaming long-response mode (512–2048 tokens). Please run both so we capture both tail and streaming behavior.
- For accurate p99 capture, please ensure the harness can replay your real request distribution (we included a simple workload.json generator in the attachment).
- We'll ask you to enable gateway-side tracing headers (traceparent/x-b3) so we can correlate traces across systems.

I'll drop the joint run invite in a minute and attach the mutual action plan.

-Marissa

- End-to-end (with our minimal enrichment): p95: 160ms, p99: 420ms

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Latency qualification & next steps (hosted vs your current provider)

Appreciate the transparency on current numbers — that's exactly the signal we need. A couple of pragmatic proposals so we can turn this into a narrow win quickly: 

1) Quick win experiment (3–5 day): Redwood hosted smoke run with your real workload (we'll provide a pre-warmed pool sized to your sustained throughput). We can aim to show p95 at or below your gateway-only p95 (85ms) for short prompts and materially reduce p99 from 420ms to under 300ms.

2) Define success criteria for the experiment:
  - Short prompt p95 <= 100ms (measured end-to-end with your harness)
  - p99 improvement >= 25% vs your end-to-end baseline
  - Streaming concurrency: sustain 40 streams with 99th-percentile frame latency < 200ms

3) If experiment succeeds, next steps: discuss reserved capacity sizing and a pilot Dedicated deployment for 90 days.

Marissa and I will coordinate the small bill-of-materials (pre-warm config, ephemeral key) so the run is frictionless. Samir/Dana — can you confirm Monday availability (2026-07-20) for a short sync and the observed run?

Best,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
